# Test fixtures

Everything the C test binaries read. All of it is checked in, so the tests run with no
network access, no model weights and no Python.

| path | read by | generated by |
|---|---|---|
| `glm_tiny/` (config.json, model.safetensors, ref.json) | `test_glm_tiny`, `test_cfg` | `tools/make_glm_tiny.py` |
| `st/` | `test_st`, `tools/verify_st.py` | `tools/make_st_fixture.py` |

## Regenerating

```bash
python tools/make_glm_tiny.py tests/fixtures/glm_tiny   # needs torch + transformers
python tools/make_st_fixture.py                         # needs numpy
```

## Why these fixtures and not simpler ones

- **`glm_tiny/`** is a random 5-layer model with the released architecture (KDA and MLA
  layers, dense and MoE feed-forward, mHC with 4 streams), stored in the released
  checkpoint's tensor names and dtypes (FP8 block-quantised, BF16, F32). `ref.json` holds
  outputs of the official transformers implementation computed from the same stored
  weights, including the DSA indexer path. Its weights are spread so every mechanism
  matters (random mHC base/scale, A_log, correction bias), and `swiglu_limit` is 0.5 so
  the SwiGLU clamp actually binds. Removing the clamp, transposing the mHC mixer or
  skipping Sinkhorn each fail the test by thousands of times the tolerance.
- **`st/`** includes a bf16 tensor with inf/NaN/-0 bit patterns, f16 subnormals, FP8
  codes with a scale grid, a rank-0 scalar, a zero-element tensor, rank-3/4 tensors, a
  name containing a quote and a backslash, `__metadata__`, and a second shard: the cases
  a hand-written header scanner gets wrong silently.
